ana: Heads-up 1: merged cust/harbor/lora-transfer-v1 and published an int4 Q4f quant build to the canary pool. Quick retrieval eval (customer quickpack) shows a strong relevance regression. Opening triage.

bryan: Can you drop the exact model tag and the eval summary?

ana: Model tag: harbor-lora-xfer-v1-q4f (LoRA transfer weights merged -> bnb q4f quant). Eval command used: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite harbor-cust-quickpack --model harbor-lora-xfer-v1-q4f --batch 192 --cache on
```
Quick numbers: recall@10 0.57 (baseline int8: 0.81), mrr 0.11 (baseline 0.23), median_latency 34ms (baseline 52ms). Many top-5 flips reported by the quickpack diff.

sima: Ouch. Any tokenizer or preprocessing changes in that PR?

ana: None 1: adapter-only merge. Quant config: 
```
quant_backend: bnb
quant_mode: q4f
adapter_only: true
per_layer_scaling: true
```
We toggled prefix cache on/off and results persisted.

eval-bot: Regression alert created: RG-2026-0820-14 (https://issues.redwood.ai/RG-2026-0820-14)

bryan: My hypothesis: bnb q4f per-layer scaling interacts badly with the low-rank adapter projections, shifting the embedding manifold. Two quick experiments to run: 1) rerun with `--quant-backend nf4` 2) q4f with `per_layer_scaling=false`. I'll queue both.

bryan: Running NF4 test now: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite harbor-cust-quickpack --model harbor-lora-xfer-v1-q4f --quant-backend nf4 --batch 192
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployment event: canary/harbor -> harbor-lora-xfer-v1-q4f (pool: canary-us-4)

bryan: NF4 run finished: recall@10 0.74, mrr 0.19, latency ~36ms. Much closer but still behind int8.

sima: Good recovery. Can you run a small layerwise ablation to see which adapter ranks are most sensitive? Use `--layer-scan` and dump distances.

bryan: Kicking a layer-scan: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite harbor-cust-quickpack --model harbor-lora-xfer-v1-q4f --quant-backend bnb --layer-scan true --output /tmp/harbor-layer-scan.json
```

maria: Quick glance at layer-scan summary: adapter projection layers 2 and 5 show the largest embedding shift under bnb-q4f with per-layer scaling enabled. The low-rank outputs in those layers have higher quantization error when bnb places per-layer scales aggressively.

sima: Does the adapter-aware quantizer help? We have that option in the quant pipeline.

bryan: I ran a small grid (q4f/nf4 x per_layer_scaling true/false x adapter-aware true/false). Short summary: best config was `quant_backend=nf4, per_layer_scaling=false` and `adapter_aware=true` combined -> recall@10 0.79, mrr 0.22, latency 38ms. That essentially matches int8 quality with ~25% lower token cost. Artifacts attached.

eval-bot: Grid artifacts uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evals/harbor/1745601234-grid-scan.json

maria: Given customer impact, recommend immediate rollback of canary to int8 and a pipeline patch to prefer nf4 or adapter-aware q4f for adapter-only LoRAs. Also add an embedding-drift gate to the LoRA onboarding quickpack CI.

bryan: I'll open a PR to add `prefer_adapter_nf4=true` in the CUST quant pipeline and include unit tests asserting recall@10 drop < 0.03 vs int8 on the harbor quickpack.

maria: I'll create the rollback deploy command: `rwi-deploy promote --model harbor-lora-xfer-v1-int8 --route canary/harbor --reason "restore retrieval quality"`

deploy-bot: Deployment promoted harbor-lora-xfer-v1-int8 -> canary/harbor (change id: DPL-11011)

sima: Bryan, can you also include the per-layer diagnostic plots in the PR so the math folks can investigate bnb scale placement? Tagging dara from infra for follow-up.

bryan: Will do. I'll also run a few random-seed reruns to ensure the nf4+adapter-aware config is stable.

eval-bot: RG-2026-0820-14 status -> triaged (severity: high)

maria: CS note draft: short customer-facing message, mitigation (we rolled back), ETA: 24-48h for patch + smoke. I'll coordinate with CS.

sima: Follow-ups: dara will own bnb per-layer scale investigation, bryan will own pipeline patch + tests, maria will coordinate CS and rollout schedule.

ana: Thanks all. Holding here until PR merges and we smoke the harbor quickpack against the canary route. End thread.
